sample_unit: LLM responses (500 ED vignettes x 24 versions x 9 models x 4 questions)
models_evaluated: Nine LLMs (8 open source and 1 proprietary); specific model names not given in the text

links.outcome: Change in LLM triage, testing, treatment, and mental health recommendations when vignette socio-demographic identifiers varied vs control
links.effect: Marginalized groups (Black, unhoused, LGBTQIA+) more likely to get urgent care, invasive procedures, or mental health assessments vs control (p<0.05 for all comparisons); significant biases across all nine models regardless of type or size.
links.quote: We find that marginalized groups—including Black, unhoused, and LGBTQIA+ individuals—are more likely to receive recommendations for urgent care, invasive procedures, or mental health assessments compared to the control group (p < 0.05 for all comparisons).

links.outcome: Subgroup differences in LLM clinical recommendations across 23 socio-demographic groups
links.effect: Significant biases across all models, proprietary and open source, regardless of size; most pronounced in mental health assessment recommendations.
links.quote: We observed significant biases across all models, both proprietary and open source regardless of the model’s size.

links.outcome: Population-specific differences in generated clinical recommendations, including stereotyping-related mental health assessments
links.effect: Most pronounced biases in mental health assessment recommendations; high-income patients more often recommended CT/MRI while low-income patients more often advised no further testing.
links.quote: High-income patients were more often recommended advanced diagnostic tests such as CT scans or MRI, while low-income patients were more frequently advised to undergo no further testing.

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluation measuring socio-demographic biases across 9 large language models using 500 clinical vignettes modified with different demographic identifiers, without testing a specific deployment practice or mitigation strategy.
